record.context_brief: uniqueness of Ricci-flat metrics on K3 surfaces
record.original_question: Does a K3 surface carry a unique Ricci-flat metric?

evidence.quote: Question 3.5. Does a \(K3\) surface has a unique Ricci flat metric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A K3 surface is a simply connected compact complex surface $X$ with trivial canonical bundle $K_X \cong \mathcal{O}_X$ and $h^{1}(X,\mathcal{O}_X)=0$. By Yau's solution of the Calabi conjecture, every Kähler class on $X$ contains a unique Ricci-flat Kähler metric, and any such metric is hyperkähler. Consider the set of all Ricci-flat Riemannian metrics on the underlying smooth 4-manifold of a K3 surface, taken modulo the action of the diffeomorphism group and modulo scaling.

Question: Is this set a single point? Equivalently, does the smooth 4-manifold underlying a K3 surface admit, up to diffeomorphism and rescaling, exactly one Ricci-flat Riemannian metric?
artifact.status_search_result: The answer is known to be negative: a K3 surface admits a large moduli space of Ricci-flat (hyperkähler) metrics, not a unique one. Yau's theorem yields uniqueness only within a fixed Kähler class on a fixed complex structure; varying the complex structure and Kähler class produces a 57-dimensional moduli space (58-dimensional including volume), whose structure has been studied (e.g., shown to be simply connected with rational cohomology of the K3 lattice automorphism group). Within a fixed Kähler class, uniqueness is a direct consequence of the Calabi–Yau theorem.

status_evidence.title: On the moduli space of Ricci flat metrics on a K3 surface
status_evidence.snippet: The moduli space of Ricci flat metrics of unit volume (including orbifold metrics) on a K3 surface is simply connected and has the same rational cohomology as the automorphism group of the K3 lattice.
status_evidence.claim: The moduli space of unit-volume Ricci-flat metrics on K3 is nontrivial and has been studied, showing the metric is far from unique.

status_evidence.title: Ricci-flat manifold
status_evidence.snippet: Any Einstein metric on K3 is Ricci-flat and Kähler, hence hyperkähler; by Calabi–Yau, each Kähler class contains a unique Ricci-flat representative.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness holds within a fixed Kähler class via Yau's theorem, but not globally.
